lit-mod-01-c5.quote: They went on to live in Trieste, Zurich, and Paris, returning to Ireland only rarely.

lit-mod-02-c1.quote: A collection of fifteen short stories set in Dublin. Ireland, between 1894 and 1905; begun in 1904 and published in Dublin in 1914.
lit-mod-02-c1.claim: Dubliners (1914): 15 short stories about Dublin life.

lit-mod-02-c3.quote: it gives a realistic portrait of the life of ordinary people living in Dublin, Ireland, on June 16, 1904. First published in its entirety in France in 1922
lit-mod-02-c3.claim: Ulysses takes place on a single day: June 16, 1904

lit-mod-03-c2.quote: In 1915, Eliot attracted widespread attention for his poem “The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock,” which was seen as a masterpiece of the Modernist movement.
lit-mod-03-c2.claim: is often called the first Modernist poem in English

lit-mod-03-c3.claim: The Waste Land (1922) is the central Modernist poem in English

lit-mod-03-c5.text: Wallace Stevens. Academy of American Poets.
lit-mod-03-c5.quote: His first book of poems, Harmonium (Alfred A. Knopf), published in 1923
lit-mod-03-c5.claim: Wallace Stevens: a Hartford insurance executive who wrote some of the most philosophical poetry in English.

lit-mod-05-c1.quote: He deposited his manuscripts with his close friend and eventual biographer, Max *Brod, and when he was dying left instructions that they were to be burnt. Brod, however, was fully aware of the importance of Kafka's work, and succeeded in getting it published.
lit-mod-05-c1.claim: asked his friend Max Brod to burn his manuscripts when he died. Brod ignored the request.

lit-mod-06-c4.quote: the imaginary Yoknapatawpha County and its inhabitants
lit-mod-06-c4.claim: wrote about Yoknapatawpha County, Mississippi: a fictional version of his actual home in Oxford.
